title: Wuerstchen: An Efficient Architecture for Large-Scale Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
layout_note: Three training stages (A, B, C) stacked as full-width horizontal bands separated by thin dashed grey rules. Each band starts with a left-hand text label ('Training of' / large 'Stage X:' / a one-line description) and then runs its own pipeline left to right. Stage A is a mirror-symmetric hourglass (image, narrowing encoder, quantizer, tokens, widening decoder, image). Stage B has two rows: the main path (encoder, latent, noising, model, output) on top and a lower conditioning branch through the Semantic Compressor that joins the model from below. Stage C has the compressor on top feeding a loss box directly, with the noising-and-model path dropped to a lower row.
grouping: No background panels or containers: the three stages are separated only by dashed horizontal rules and named by large left-hand labels. Colour families carry component identity across bands: the Stage A encoder's light green frustum reappears unchanged in Stage B, and the pale peach Semantic Compressor frustum appears in both Stage B and Stage C. Small connector operations (resize, 1x1 conv) share a pale yellow fill; both loss boxes share a bright teal fill; both noising steps share a light grey box.
shapes_depth: Pseudo-3-D throughout. Encoders, decoder and the Semantic Compressor are translucent truncated pyramids (frustums) that narrow or widen in the flow direction to show down- or up-sampling. Input and output images are photo thumbnails drawn as slanted slabs with a light blue edge. Latents and tokens are small 3-D cubes tiled with multicolour cells. The quantizer and noising steps are shaded 3-D boxes; the Stage B model is a large yellow 3-D U-Net-like block with a notched top, and the Stage C model is a large slate-purple 3-D cuboid, the darkest fill in the figure. Loss and connector operations are flat small rounded rectangles. Arrows are thin black lines with elbow routes for the loss and conditioning paths.
proposed_highlight: The two diffusion models are the largest shapes in their bands and carry the largest text in the figure ('Model' set much bigger than any other label, followed by its italic symbol), each in its own fill: pale yellow in Stage B, and in Stage C a slate purple that is darker than every other pastel fill. The paper's Semantic Compressor is drawn as a distinct pale peach frustum annotated with its downsampling factor (f32), set against the light green f4 encoder, and each stage is named in large type at the left edge of its band.
lesson: For a multi-stage training figure, give each stage its own full-width band under a dashed rule and redraw a module that is reused across stages with the same shape and fill colour in every band, so the reader can track the reused parts without separate frozen or shared markers.
notes: Venue ICLR 2024 from the arXiv journal_ref (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref), verified by the scout. Tensor sizes are written on arrows and along image edges (e.g. 1024 / 1024 / 3 on the input image, 4x256x256, 1280x24x24, 16x24x24), and module labels carry italic math symbols and a downsampling factor in parentheses (f4, f32). 'text-conditioning' enters as a plain-text label with an arrow into each model. The refs crop record lists five embedded raster images (the photo thumbnails), which kb measure excludes from the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: three training stages stacked as horizontal bands separated by grey rules (Stage A VQGAN reconstruction, Stage B latent image decoder, Stage C text-conditional generation), each read left to right

relations.form: three full-width bands top to bottom with large 'Training of Stage A/B/C' titles on the left
Stage A: image -> green trapezoid encoder f_Theta -> blue Quantizer Q -> coloured token cube -> lilac decoder -> image
the green f_Theta encoder from Stage A reappears in Stage B, and the peach Semantic Compressor e_phi appears in both Stage B and Stage C, drawn in the same shape and fill
in Stage B the compressed semantic code C_sc (through a 1x1 conv) and text-conditioning arrive from below into the yellow Model f_theta, which also takes the noised latents from the left
in Stages B and C a green 'diffusion loss' box sits above the model, with a line from the clean latent on the left and a line from the model output on the right meeting in it

channels.colour: fill = component identity (green VQGAN encoder, lilac decoder, blue quantizer, peach semantic compressor, yellow Stage B model, purple Stage C model, grey latent noising, teal-green loss); multicolour cubes = latent tensors
channels.shape: 3-D trapezoids/frusta = encoders/decoders with resolution change, flat image tiles = images, cubes = latent tensors, flat boxes = operations or losses
channels.line: solid black arrows only, with tensor sizes as labels
channels.frame: no enclosing frames; thin grey horizontal rules separate the stages

quality.strengths: Reused components keep their shape and fill across stages (f_Theta in A and B, e_phi in B and C), so the cascade's reuse reads without labels; tensor shapes are written on the wires (4x256x256, 16x24x24); both sides of each diffusion loss are drawn.
quality.weaknesses: The diffusion-loss inputs run on long lines that rise above the model and back down; the Stage B and Stage C models differ only in fill and could be mistaken for unrelated networks; the text-conditioning in Stage B enters from below via a long multi-segment path.

insights.structure: Three full-width horizontal bands (Training of Stage A / B / C) separated by dashed grey rules, each with a large left-hand stage label and its own left-to-right pipeline; Stage A is a mirror-symmetric hourglass, Stages B and C split into a main row and a second row for the Semantic Compressor or noising path.
insights.data: Input and output images are photo thumbnails drawn as slanted slabs with pixel sizes written along their edges (1024/1024/3, 768/768/3), latents and VQ tokens are small 3-D cubes tiled with multicolour cells, and tensor shapes (4x256x256, 1280x24x24, 16x24x24) are written on the arrows.
insights.emphasis: Each band's diffusion model is the largest shape with the largest label ('Model' plus italic symbol): a pale-yellow notched U-Net-like block in Stage B and a slate-purple cuboid in Stage C, the darkest fill in the figure; encoders and the Semantic Compressor are translucent frustums whose narrowing shows the downsampling factor (f4, f32).
insights.flow: Each band reads left to right; loss paths leave the latent cube, run up and across to a teal 'diffusion loss' box above the model and back down from the output, and the conditioning branch (Semantic Compressor -> 1x1 conv -> c_sc) enters the Stage B model from below with text-conditioning joining it.
insights.avoid: The same role gets different fills across bands (yellow model in B, purple in C) and the Stage A band draws no loss at all; small connector labels (1024->786 in a pale-yellow box, against 768 written on the Stage C image) are tiny and visibly inconsistent.

arrangement.units: three unboxed full-width horizontal bands divided by dashed rules, each one training stage with a large text label at its left edge
arrangement.inputs_as: photo thumbnail drawn as a slanted 3-D slab with its pixel size on the edges
arrangement.losses_at: top of each band (teal 'diffusion loss' box above the model, Stages B and C)
arrangement.shared: modules reused across bands keep the same frustum shape and fill (light-green f4 encoder in A and B, peach Semantic Compressor in B and C)
